topic: Structures and Properties of Ionic, Covalent, and Metallic Substances
key_concepts: Properties of materials depend on atom arrangement and bond type
Ionic compounds form by electron transfer from a metal to a nonmetal
Ionic compounds exist as extended 3D arrays of alternating cations and anions
NaCl is a formula unit, not a molecule
Electrostatic attractions hold ions together in ionic crystals
Ball-and-stick and space-filling models represent ionic crystal lattices
When NaCl dissolves in water, water molecules release Na+ and Cl- ions, not atoms
Covalent compounds form individual molecules from nonmetals
Within water molecules atoms are held by covalent bonds
Between water molecules weak intermolecular interactions hold molecules together
Frozen water is a molecular crystal with molecules in a hexagonal arrangement
Table sugar is covalent because all its atoms are nonmetals
